textbookText: 5. Write down any two differences between monohybrid cross and dihybrid cross.
Ans:- The differences between monohybrid cross and dihybrid cross are
Monohybrid cross
Dihybrid cross
Monohybrid cross involves one pair of contrasting characters.
Dihybrid cross involves two pairs.
The genotypic ratio of monohybrid cross is 1:2:1
The genotypic ratio of dihybrid cross is 3:1.
6. Write any two differences between first generation (F1) and second generation (F2).
Ans:-The differences between first generation (F1) and second generation (F2) are
First generation (F1)
Second generation (F2)
F₁ generation is obtained by crossing two pure parents.
F₂ generation is obtained by selfing F₁ plants.
F₁ plants are all similar.
F₂ plants show both dominant and recessive traits.
7. Write two probable causes that Mendel did not do his experiment in frog instead of pea.
Ans:- Two probable causes that Mendel did not do his experiment in frog instead of pea are
i) Frog takes a long time to reproduce, while pea plant reproduces quickly.
ii) Frog breeding is difficult to control, but pea plants can be easily self- or cross-pollinated.
8. State any two difficulties Mendel would have faced if he had carried his experiment on human instead of pea plant.
Ans:- Two difficulties Mendel would have faced if he had carried his experiment on human instead of pea plant are
i) Humans have a long generation time.
ii) Ethical and moral issues prevent experimental breeding in humans.

10. When a pure pea plant with red flower is crossed with pure pea plant with white flower, what will be the characteristics of
offspring in first filial generation? Explain with reason.
Ans:- When a pure pea plant with red flowers is crossed with a pure pea plant with white flowers, all the offspring in the first
filial (F₁) generation have red flowers. This is because the gene for red color is dominant over the gene for white color, which
is recessive.
11. Offspring obtained from same parents show some similarities but they are not exactly similar to each other. Why? Write
with reason.
Ans:- Offspring obtained from the same parents show similarities but are not exactly the same because of genetic variation.
During meiosis and fertilization, recombination and random assortment of chromosomes occur, producing unique gene
combinations.
12. In a cross between long wined Drosophila with short Drosophila only long winged Drosophila were seen in F1
generation. Write its reason.
Ans:- In a cross between long-winged and short-winged Drosophila, only long-winged flies appear in the F₁ generation
because the gene for long wings is dominant over the gene for short wings.

15. Offspring have the same characteristics as their parents. Why?
Ans:- Offspring have the same characteristics as their parents because they inherit genes from their parents. These genes are
passed through DNA, which carries hereditary information.
